title: Exclusive / AI is an inflation problem, Fed’s Goolsbee says
key_facts: Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, told Semafor's Compound Interest podcast that AI-linked inflation is 'jumping out of its lane' and pushing up prices in unrelated parts of the economy.
He said he is 'getting increasingly nervous that that's just straight, old-fashioned overheating demand'.
Prices for land, electricity, water, construction and electrical parts used in data centres have surged but have not yet clearly reached consumer items such as groceries or a haircut (Semafor).
US inflation was 3.4% in August; September's figures are due this week (Semafor).

Goolsbee is not on the Fed's rate-setting committee but joins it in 2027; asked about another rate rise at the Fed's meeting later this month he said 'If inflation remains persistent, then I think it's clear what the Fed has to do'.
He said he does not know the percentages, that oil and tariffs also play a part, and that AI has not overheated demand in aggregate 'but it's starting to'; unemployment is 4.2%.
Fed Governor Lisa Cook warned last month of 'some economy-wide pressure from AI-fueled demand' but said so far it looks like a shift in demand toward AI-related sectors.
quote_evidence: Inflation tied to the AI boom is 'jumping out of its lane' and starting to push up prices in unrelated corners of the economy, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said.
I'm getting increasingly nervous that that's just straight, old-fashioned overheating demand.
If inflation remains persistent, then I think it's clear what the Fed has to do.
why_it_matters_hint: A Federal Reserve official links the AI building boom to wider price rises, which bears on whether interest rates go up again.
